record.title: AlphaGenome 2 reports higher cell-type-specific variant recall in genomic benchmarks
record.summary: Google DeepMind announced AlphaGenome 2, a genomic sequence model that conditions predictions on a target tissue, cell type or cell state. In the linked manuscript, the authors report that on the TenK10K single-cell eQTL causality task it reached 30% recall at 90% precision, compared with 16% for AlphaGenome 1 fine-tuned on single-cell data; reported overall AUPRC was 0.76 versus 0.72 for that baseline and 0.69 for Scooby. The authors also report higher recall for cell-type eQTL sign prediction. These are first-party computational results on existing datasets, not an independent reproduction or new wet-lab validation. The API is offered for non-commercial research; model source code and weights are planned for final publication. The authors state that the system is not validated for clinical or diagnostic use.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Google DeepMind announced AlphaGenome 2 on 2026-11-11 and linked a full manuscript describing the model and its evaluations.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: At 90% precision on the TenK10K single-cell eQTL causality task, the authors report recall of 30% for AlphaGenome 2 versus 16% for AlphaGenome 1 fine-tuned on single-cell data (AG1-sc); reported overall AUPRC is 0.76 versus 0.72 for AG1-sc and 0.69 for Scooby.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: At the same benchmark, the authors report TenK10K single-cell eQTL sign-prediction recall of 43% for AlphaGenome 2 versus 23% for AG1-sc at 90% accuracy; overall AUC is 0.85 versus 0.79 and 0.77, respectively.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper describes a model that conditions 1-Mb human or mouse DNA sequence on a target tissue, cell type or cell state. It reports training on bulk and single-cell datasets, including 107 million human single-cell RNA-sequencing profiles, and says the API is available for non-commercial research; model source code and weights are planned for final publication.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The results were not independently reproduced in this activation. The paper reports no new wet-lab experiments, says high-precision recall remains a minority for fine-mapped eQTLs and putative GWAS variants, and states that AlphaGenome 2 has not been validated or approved for clinical or diagnostic use.

evidence_gaps.description: The TenK10K metrics and other reported evaluations were not independently reproduced in this activation.
The linked manuscript says model source code and weights will be released upon final publication; this activation did not test the non-commercial API.
The results use computational benchmarks on existing datasets and do not demonstrate causal biological effects, clinical validity or patient outcomes.
The authors report that high-precision recall remains low for fine-mapped eQTLs and putative GWAS variants and that transient, stimulated and disease cell states are underrepresented.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported cell-type-specific variant-prediction gains generalize, researchers could prioritize candidate regulatory variants and their relevant cell states more effectively across human genetics studies. The consequence is notable for computational genomics, while the paper reports no new wet-lab experiments and does not claim clinical validation.
limitations: The reported performance figures are first-party manuscript results and were not independently reproduced by the research desk.
The study reports no new wet-lab experiments; its cell-level predictions are computational analyses on previously collected datasets.

The authors state that high-precision recall recovers only a minority of fine-mapped eQTLs and putative causal GWAS variants; results can be weaker outside accessible chromatin and for post-transcriptional mechanisms.
Transient, stimulated and disease states are underrepresented; observational condition embeddings encode correlations, not causal relationships.

The API is offered for non-commercial research. The model source code and weights are planned for final publication. The authors state that the model is not validated or approved for clinical or diagnostic use.

technical.claimed_result: On TenK10K single-cell eQTL causality, the authors report recall of 30% versus 16% for AG1-sc at 90% precision and overall AUPRC of 0.76 versus 0.72 for AG1-sc and 0.69 for Scooby. On sign prediction they report recall of 43% versus 23% for AG1-sc at 90% accuracy and overall AUC of 0.85 versus 0.79 and 0.77.
technical.demonstrated_result: Google DeepMind published an announcement and linked a full manuscript specifying the architecture, training data, evaluation datasets, baselines, reported metrics and limitations. the research desk did not independently reproduce the reported results.
technical.mechanism: AlphaGenome 2 takes a 1-Mb DNA sequence and a condition describing a tissue, cell type or state. It modulates sequence representations using that condition and can infer a condition embedding from single-cell gene-expression data to make predictions for unseen datasets or states.
technical.regime: The model accepts a 1-Mb human or mouse DNA sequence and a biological condition. The TenK10K benchmark covers single-cell expression QTLs across 28 peripheral-blood cell types and single-cell chromatin-accessibility QTLs across 24 cell types. Comparisons include AlphaGenome 1 fine-tuned on single-cell data (AG1-sc) and Scooby.
technical.strongest_baseline: For the quoted TenK10K recall comparison, AG1-sc is the closest within-family comparator: AlphaGenome 1 fine-tuned on single-cell data. The paper also compares against Scooby, a specialized sequence-to-function model. These are author-run manuscript results, not independently replicated here.

brief.title: AlphaGenome 2 reports higher cell-type-specific variant recall in genomic benchmarks
brief.why_it_matters: Regulatory variants can act differently across cell types, while large single-cell maps rarely include enough donors for direct variant association tests. If the reported gains hold up, conditioning on cell state could help researchers prioritize candidate variants and where to study them. The paper’s computational results do not establish causal biology, clinical utility or improved patient outcomes.
